# The overflow-menu spec snapshots its partition before the menu owns it

## Context

A v13.3.1 AC-2 roving specimen ([D#19994 discussioncomment-19133550](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19994#discussioncomment-19133550), cut record #20022). `WorkstationMaximizeOverflowMenuNL` › "docked control arm: clicking More tabs keeps the overflow menu open, focused, and partition-stable until selection" went red in a full `e2e/workstation` + `e2e/dashboard` run and is green alone. The `appliedHiddenIds` assertion passed. The visible-headers assertion failed: with the menu open, the DOM showed one header fewer while the plugin's `appliedHiddenIds` still equalled the pre-open set. The cut lead's triage: one ticket per cause.

**Observed** (Vega's run): the red and its signature. **Not retained:** which header vanished. **Measured** (6× CPU throttle, AC-2): two mechanisms, below.

## The Problem

> **Corrected 2026-10-23, before any PR, per AC-2's own clause.** The first version inferred one cause from a code read. The throttled measurement confirmed it and found a second, more frequent one that the inferred fix does not cover. Both pass the worker-only gate, and neither is a product defect.

`waitForOverflowSettled` gates the pre-open snapshot on worker flags only: `measuring === false`, `projectQueued === false`, and a non-empty `appliedHiddenIds`. It then reads the DOM-visible headers and compares them, and `appliedHiddenIds`, with the open-menu state.

**(A) The DOM lags the published split.** This is the specimen's signature. `Overflow#project` calls `applySplit`, which hides headers through `button.hidden = true`, a vdom update it does not await, and sets `appliedHiddenIds` synchronously. `project()` then releases `measuring` in its `finally`. So the gate can pass while a header's removal is still in flight. The snapshot then lists a header the worker already treats as hidden. With the menu open it vanishes, and `appliedHiddenIds` stays the same. Measured in one of three instrumented runs: `neo-tab-header-button-5` was in the applied set (11 ids) and still rendered at the snapshot.

**(B) The strip re-partitions after the gate and before the menu opens.** The spec's pane-body click reveals the focus-gated actions in the DOM. The plugin learns their width only from their own `resize` events (`Toolbar#onActionResize` → `actionGeometryChange` → `Overflow#onActionGeometryChange`). Under load those events can arrive after the gate has seen an idle plugin.

Instrumented run: the last pass before the snapshot measured one action (the 24 px control) for a 355 px extent and hid 10 tabs. About 400 ms later on the app-worker clock, the four revealed actions' resizes arrived; the next pass measured 120 px of actions, a 259 px extent, and hid 11. That was still before the menu opened, so the menu opened with 11 items against a 10-id snapshot.

On `dev` at 6× this fails the docked arm 8/8, at `itemCount`. No DOM gate can see it, because nothing in the worker or the DOM marks a resize that has not been delivered.

A re-partition while the menu is closed is legitimate. An open menu parks every projection: `applySplit` has one caller, behind `queueOpenMenuProjection`. So the partition the contract protects is the one the menu opened against, not a pre-click read.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`:
  - `applySplit` sets `button.hidden` / `button.show()` per header, then `me.appliedHiddenIds = [...hidden]`. `project()`'s `finally` sets `me.measuring = false`, and `publishProjectionState()` fires `overflowProjectionIdle`.
  - `onActionGeometryChange` projects on each action's rendered resize.
  - `queueOpenMenuProjection` parks every projection while the menu is shown or mounted.
- `src/toolbar/Base.mjs`: `onActionResize` fires `actionGeometryChange` from each action root's DOM `resize`.
- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationMaximizeOverflowMenuNL.spec.mjs`: `waitForOverflowSettled` reads only the plugin's state. `assertOverflowMenuHoldsAndSelects` snapshots `appliedHiddenIds` and `preVisibleHeaders` before clicking the control.
- Precedent: #20020 / PR #20021 settled `WorkstationTabDragHeadersStayNL` on the DOM and the worker state together.

## The Fix

Spec-only.

- `waitForOverflowSettled` also polls until the DOM shows `appliedHiddenIds`: a hidden id has no rendered box, and every other id has one. This covers (A).
- `assertOverflowMenuHoldsAndSelects` takes the partition snapshot (`appliedHiddenIds` and the visible headers) once the menu is visible and settled, then holds 350 ms and compares. This covers (B). The focus-gated action ids stay compared with the pre-click read, because focus never leaves the pane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both arms take their partition snapshot once the menu is open and the DOM shows `appliedHiddenIds`. The action ids stay compared with the pre-click read.
- [ ] At 6× CPU throttle (the instrument #18721 used), the docked arm reproduces the red on `dev` with its mechanism recorded (vanished header inside or outside `appliedHiddenIds`). With the fix, both arms are green N/N, and the maximized arm still goes red with #19984's `DomAccess` fix reversed. *(Amended 2026-10-23: the original asked only for the inside-the-set signature.)*
- [ ] A disposition naming the cause is recorded on #20022 for the AC-2 line.

## Out of Scope

Whether `overflowProjectionIdle` / `whenProjectionIdle` should wait for the DOM or for undelivered action resizes. Both production consumers (the dock `MotionSignal` and the tab `SortZone` drag start) read that edge. A drag parks projections itself (`queueSortDragProjection`). It becomes its own ticket only if a falsifier shows a consumer harmed.
